topics.label: Super Visa for Parents
topics.seoTitle: Super Visa for Parents Canada 2026 | CMG
topics.metaDescription: Super Visa as an alternative or complement to PGP sponsorship — extended visits for parents without the lottery wait.
topics.lead: For parents who aren't selected in the PGP lottery, or families who want an interim option, the Super Visa allows extended visits of up to 5 years per entry — without requiring the sponsor to win a randomized selection process first.
headings: Super Visa vs. PGP — For Parents Specifically

topics.label: Orphaned Relatives
topics.metaDescription: Sponsor an orphaned relative (sibling, nephew, niece, or grandchild) for Canadian PR — eligibility criteria explained.
topics.lead: In specific circumstances, Canadian citizens and permanent residents can sponsor an orphaned relative — such as a sibling, nephew, niece, or grandchild — who is under a set age threshold, unmarried, and has no surviving parent, or whose parents have separately abandoned them.

topics.label: Minimum Necessary Income
topics.seoTitle: Minimum Necessary Income for Sponsorship Canada 2026 | CMG
topics.metaDescription: How Canada calculates the sponsor income threshold (LICO +30%) for PGP applications, and what documentation proves it.
topics.lead: The Minimum Necessary Income is the income threshold sponsors must meet for certain family sponsorship categories, most notably the Parents and Grandparents Program — based on the Low Income Cut-Off (LICO) plus a 30% buffer, scaled to household size.

topics.label: Sponsorship Eligibility
topics.metaDescription: Who can sponsor a family member for Canadian PR: citizenship/PR status, age, undertaking obligations, and disqualifying factors.
topics.lead: Before assessing any specific relationship, every sponsorship application starts with confirming the sponsor themselves is eligible — a distinct set of criteria from what's required of the person being sponsored.

topics.label: Sponsorship Processing Times
topics.seoTitle: Family Sponsorship Processing Times Canada 2026 | CMG
topics.metaDescription: Current expected processing times for spousal, PGP, and dependent child sponsorship applications, and what affects them.
topics.lead: Processing times for family sponsorship vary meaningfully by category and application completeness — spousal applications typically move fastest, while PGP applications carry the added lottery-selection step before processing even begins.

topics.label: Sponsorship Appeal
topics.metaDescription: Appealing a refused sponsorship to the Immigration Appeal Division: grounds, timeline, and what evidence strengthens an appeal.
topics.lead: Most refused sponsorship applications — spousal sponsorship in particular — can be appealed to the Immigration Appeal Division (IAD), which independently reviews the evidence and can overturn the original refusal.

topics.label: Adult Grant of Citizenship
topics.seoTitle: Adult Grant of Canadian Citizenship 2026 | CMG
topics.metaDescription: Standard adult citizenship application: physical presence, tax filing, language, and knowledge test requirements. Free eligibility check.
topics.lead: This is the standard route to Canadian citizenship for permanent residents aged 18 and over — requiring a set period of physical presence in Canada, tax compliance, and, for most applicants, a language and knowledge test.

topics.label: Minor Grant of Citizenship
topics.seoTitle: Minor Grant of Canadian Citizenship 2026 | CMG
topics.metaDescription: Citizenship application process for permanent resident children under 18 — simplified requirements compared to the adult grant.
topics.lead: Permanent resident children under 18 can apply for Canadian citizenship through a simplified process that doesn't require the language or knowledge test adult applicants must complete, though a parent or legal guardian must typically apply on the child's behalf.
headings: Key Differences From the Adult Grant
